page.layout: One block of running text, with notes in the left margin. No notes below the text. Running head above the text, page number at the head.

main_text.p: a Clem. Alex. orat. adhort. ad Gent. ex Posidippo.quæ dilexit, imagine: b Herodot. in Euterp. Pomponi. Mela lib.1.a Venerem Praxiteles Cratinæ, amicæ suæ, specie effinxit; & statuarii Athenis Alcibiadis forma Mercurios expresse-runt. b Ægyptii autem, non modo bestias animatas, sed etiam inanimas earum effigies adorabant.

c Iuv.sat.ij.[?]c Quis nescit, Volusi Bithynice, qualia demes Ægyptus portenta colat? crocodilon adorat Pars hæc; illa pavet saiurâ serpentibus ibin: Effigies sacri nitet aurea cercopitheci, Dimidio magicæ resonat ubi Menone chordæ, Atq; vetus Thebe centū iacet obruta portus:

d Plin. hist. nat.l.6.c.29.& d in Rhadatensi urbe felis aurea pro Deo colebatur. Vtriusque vero generis imagines idola vocat Paulus, quum {e}Iudæum ait abominari {1}illa idola. e Rom. 2.22.1 τὰ εἴδωλα.

Quemadmodum & rursus idolorum nomine designat statuas hominum, ubi {f}Corinthios, quando Gentes erant, ad idola muta abreptos esse dicit: sive se Græcis illi conformabant, inter quos degebant; sive Romanis, {g}a'quibus genus ducebant. f1.Cor.12.2.g Pausan. Corinthiacis. Dio, hist. Rom.lib.43.Quamobrem imagines hominum & bestiarum, id est, verarum rerum similitudines, Scriptura sine omni dubitatione idola sæpe nominat.

3 At enim Bellarminus negat has imagines fuisse rerum verarum, quoniam a Gentilibus ad repræsentandos falsos Deos adhibebantur. Quem in finem adjicit: Scriptura nusquam tribuit nomen idoli ullive ræ imagini, sed solum simulacris Gentilium, quæ falsos Deos referebant. At istud enuntiatum, ex parte sophisticam vanitatem occultit, {h}modo patefactâ: Huius libri cap.2.§.6.ex parte captiosâ calumniam geminocumulat e-vidente mendacio. Vno, quòd affirmat nomè idoli simulacris solùm Gentilium tribui à Scriptura: quasi

page.notes: Printed page 364; running head and page number read clearly. Handwritten underlining on the lines "Ægyptii autem", "Vtriusque vero generis imagines", "id est, verarum rerum similitudines, Scriptura sine omni dubitatione" and "Vno, quòd" is not print and is left out. Doubtful readings: "luæ" read as suæ (long s); "fiue" / "sivese" read as "siue se"; "saiurâ" possibly saturâ; "portus" as printed (Juvenal has portis); "Menone" as printed; "felis" possibly with a long-s form; Greek note "τὰ εἴδωλα" uncertain; left-margin reference "Iuv.sat.ij." uncertain; the mark before "Huius libri" reads "ij" in the margin, and I matched it to text mark h, which may be wrong; "Atq;" as printed. The catchword "Iudæ-" is at the right below the last full line.
